question: Which metric is most commonly used by Antibiotic Stewardship Programmes (ASPs) to quantify antibiotic consumption across an institution?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. DDD/100 bed-days is the WHO-recommended metric for comparing antibiotic consumption between wards and institutions; it standardises for patient volume.

answers.text: Number of antibiotic prescriptions written per month

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This does not account for dose size or duration, making inter-institutional comparison unreliable.

answers.text: Cost of antibiotics purchased per financial quarter

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Cost reflects pricing variability, not actual consumption volume or appropriateness of use.
This tracks outpatient continuation but not in-hospital consumption intensity.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the stewardship metrics section. ASPs use WHO-defined DDD/100 bed-days as the primary consumption indicator.
Well done. DDD/100 bed-days is the international standard process metric for antibiotic stewardship surveillance.
